newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries dip pulls emerging debt lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries dip pulls emerging debt lower.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices slid lower on the heels of another decline in U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
Spreads over Treasuries generally widened -- particularly in Ecuador, where uncertainty lingered over potential resignations in the country's economic leadership.
In late trading, Ecuador PDIs were off 1-1/2 at 64-5/8 bid, and their spread was about 22 basis points wider.

Ecuador Finance Minister Carlos Davalos submitted his resignation on Thursday. But it remained unclear whether President Fabian Alarcon would accept the resignation and whether other economy team members would follow suit.
Traders said a large volume of Ecuador paper had sold, but they added that many players were still on the sidelines awaiting further developments.
"We're waiting to find out whether these are real resignations or if it's just a ploy by these guys to get through more-drastic fiscal cuts," one trader said.

U.S. analysts said Davalos's bid to resign signaled a rift between the economic team and the president. Later, Alarcon issued a statement acknowledging the move by Davalos, although he stopped short of accepting the resignation.
Resignation of central bank head Fidel Jaramillo -- reported in the local press early in the day and later denied by an aide -- would be a more serious setback, traders said.

In Mexican debt, rumors of an impending ratings upgrade briefly pushed prices higher. But David Beers, head of sovereign ratings at Standard & Poor's, said talk S&P would up Mexico's BB long-term foreign currency rating was "not true".
Discounting of the rumor brought the country's debt back into negative territory, with Mexico pars off 3/8 at 77-1/8 late in the session.
Joyce Chang, emerging market debt strategist at Merrill Lynch, said she did not expect S&P to change its stable ratings outlook for Mexico until well after the July elections.
"S&P has emphasized they want to see how the PRI works with the opposition parties on issues such as tax reform," she said.
Talk of a Venezuela Brady bond buyback continued to swirl, but Venezuela FLIRBs followed the market lower, trading off 1/4 at 92-7/8.
"I wouldn't view (buyback rumors) as something that's much of a surprise," Chang said. "(Venezuela has) been very public in saying they want to do something like that."
"Elsewhere, Brazil "C" bonds were off 1/2 at 80-1/8, and Argentina FRBs were down 1/8 at 93-5/8.
Poland priced its first Yankee bond, a $400 million issue, on Thursday.
Poland Brady bonds sold lower, with PDIs off 5/8 at 85-5/8 bid.
